Type files from their bytes and their names

Source: R/type.R
mime_type.Rd

Reads the first bytes of each path in one C loop, types them as mime_sniff() does, guesses a type from the name as mime_guess() does, and says whether the two agree. The other columns answer what a consumer asks before opening a file: what a compressed file holds, whether it is encrypted or truncated, its line endings, and a script's interpreter.

Usage

mime_type(
  path,
  limit = 4096L,
  complete = FALSE,
  inner = c("name", "decompress"),
  text = c("whatwg", "family"),
  charset = c("declared", "detect"),
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

A character vector of paths.

limit

The number of bytes to read from each file; 0 reads whole files.

complete

If TRUE, also read each file's end and fill complete: a ZIP needs its end-of-central-directory record, a PDF %%EOF in its last kilobyte, a gzip stream must inflate to its trailer, and Parquet must end in PAR1. Other formats give NA. A PDF is encrypted when its trailer dictionary, found in the last 4 KB, names /Encrypt.

inner

How to find the type inside a compression wrapper (gzip, bzip2, xz, zstd, LZ4, lzip, compress): "name" takes it from the rest of the name, so data.csv.gz holds text/csv; "decompress" decompresses gzip with zukomp and sniffs the result, falling back to the name for other wrappers and for files over 16 MiB.

text

"whatwg" keeps the standard's answer for text; "family" offers a still generic text/plain to the family's sniffers, which read whole files.

charset

"declared" reports the charset the bytes declare; "detect" asks zuutf where they declare none, or only the C1 guess.

strict

If TRUE, an unreadable path raises zumime_io_error.

Value

A zumime_result data frame with one row per path and columns path, type, confidence, charset, by_name, agree, inner, encrypted, complete, newline and interpreter.

Details

Unreadable and missing paths give a row with type NA and confidence "none", so one bad entry does not abort a scan of a tree; strict = TRUE raises zumime_io_error instead. A directory is inode/directory, and nothing is read from it.

agree is TRUE when the byte type and the name type lie on one lineage, so bytes that say text/plain agree with a .csv name and a ZIP agrees with a .docx name; FALSE when they differ, such as a PNG named .txt; and NA when either is unknown. A disagreement is a finding, not an error.

The default answer depends on nothing outside the package. Three arguments ask for an optional family package. inner = "decompress" uses zukomp and charset = "detect" uses zuutf; either raises zumime_dependency_error when its package is absent. text = "family" never raises: it uses whichever of zucsv, zujson and zutoml are installed, listed by zumime_info()$family, and with none it keeps the standard's answer. zuutf and zutoml are not yet on CRAN; install them from GitHub. An error inside an optional package leaves that answer as it was, so a corrupt stream keeps the name's inner.

See also

mime_sniff() for bytes and the standard's contexts, mime_check() for an allowlist.

Examples

dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)
writeLines(c("a,b", "1,2"), file.path(dir, "data.csv"))
saveRDS(mtcars, file.path(dir, "cars.rds"))
writeBin(
  as.raw(c(0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a)),
  file.path(dir, "logo.txt")
)
mime_type(list.files(dir, full.names = TRUE))
#> <zumime_result: 3 rows>
#>                                        path              type confidence
#> 1 /tmp/RtmpOgFnor/file1afe6ba2d91e/cars.rds application/x-rds   definite
#> 2 /tmp/RtmpOgFnor/file1afe6ba2d91e/data.csv        text/plain   probable
#> 3 /tmp/RtmpOgFnor/file1afe6ba2d91e/logo.txt         image/png   definite
#>   charset           by_name agree inner encrypted complete newline interpreter
#> 1    <NA> application/x-rds  TRUE  <NA>        NA       NA    <NA>        <NA>
#> 2   UTF-8          text/csv  TRUE  <NA>        NA       NA      lf        <NA>
#> 3    <NA>        text/plain FALSE  <NA>        NA       NA    <NA>        <NA>
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
